messages:
harry: PSA — my toaster just shorted during breakfast and somehow took out my office ethernet switch. lost connection mid-standup, apologies for the awkward silence. toaster is now in the trash 
jess: omg that is peak WFH chaos 
omeera: wait — toaster? did it trip the breaker or just the switch reboot?
harry: breaker didn't trip, but the little unmanaged switch blinked all its LEDs then came back up ~90s later. lost a bunch of SSH sessions.
otto: do you have a UPS on the switch or is it just wall-warted?
harry: wall-warted. cheap 5-port from a yard sale. never thought about it until now.
jess: yard-sale ethernet switch + toaster = iconic.
netbot: [automated] At 2345678910 detected short power dip on building circuit B3. Affected devices: outlet 12, smartPDU group "apt-b3" reported undervoltage event duration ~1.3s. No building-wide breaker trip recorded.
omeera: that explains it. undervoltage can make little PSUs brown out and reboot gear.
otto: pro move: get a small UPS for the switch + cable modem. even a 300-600VA backup will ride through toaster burps.
harry: short poll: recommended mitigation? (1) move to different outlet + UPS, (2) replace cheap switch with better PSU, (3) keep living dangerously. vote 1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣
jess: 1️⃣ — UPS + move
omeera: 2️⃣ — new switch with better regulator
otto: 1️⃣ + add smart strip, also label the toaster drawer 
harry: thanks y'all. ordered a small UPS and a decent 8-port switch. also unplugging the toaster when not in use from now on 
netbot: [reminder] Building maintenance note: landlord scheduled wiring inspection for corridor B3 on 2345679500 UTC. Expect brief outages if landlord accesses panel.
jess: please include before/after pic of the new setup for the WFH horrors gallery 
harry: will do — hopefully future me will be less crunchy and more connected :coffee:
